These pathways indicate that Isotrifoliol may exert its biological effects through multiple intermediaries, ultimately influencing Cytochrome c4. The scores from the two paths suggest a moderate level of confidence in the relationship, with slight variations in the strength of the evidence. The integration of these pathways highlights the possibility of a complex regulatory mechanism involving chemokines and their downstream targets. The evidence supports a plausible pathway, but further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct interaction between Isotrifoliol and Cytochrome c4.
